features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Experience shipping AI or LLM systems in real production settings, especially with attention to reliability, evaluation, or hardening.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Academic preparation
features.description: The level of formal relevant technical education or degree attainment the letter presents.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Direct experience designing or owning agent-based systems with explicit boundaries, guardrails, orchestration, or supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering improvements or problem solving.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Collaboration and learning posture
features.description: Humility, coachability, and willingness to partner with security specialists or deepen expertise through collaboration.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Whether the letter frames security tooling as helping developers adopt safer behavior through better defaults, lower friction, and user empathy.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: The extent to which the letter substantiates claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, scope, or owned details rather than broad assertions.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists qualities or interests with little supporting evidence.
Includes a few examples but limited detail on ownership or effect.
Gives concrete examples of work with enough detail to make the claims credible.
Repeatedly ties claims to specific actions and clear outcomes or impact.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How central and substantial Go appears as a production backend language in the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: Does not provide meaningful evidence of Go use.
Mentions some Go exposure but not as a core language.
Presents Go as a major working language in production.
Presents Go as the principal or dominant language across core services.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: How clearly the letter states the outcomes, effects, or operational consequences of the applicant's work rather than just listing responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: Lists responsibilities or technologies without explaining what changed because of the work.
Suggests benefit, but the outcome remains vague or implied.
Gives a clear before-and-after or operational result, such as a queue becoming routed, a bottleneck disappearing, or hours being saved.
Shows strong leverage-oriented impact articulation, tying the work to measurable capacity, broad downstream benefit, or a transformed operating model.

features.name: Language breadth
features.description: The range of programming languages the letter shows beyond the core required language stack.

levels.descriptor: Shows narrow breadth beyond the main language or two.
Shows moderate breadth across several additional languages.
Shows very broad breadth across many additional languages.

features.name: Narrative quality
features.description: The coherence, distinctiveness, voice, and flow of the letter as a persuasive story rather than a checklist.

levels.descriptor: Reads as transactional or template-like, with little memorable voice.
Clear and competent but conventional.
Has a noticeable voice or coherent personal arc that helps the reader remember the candidate.
Uses distinctive framing and a well-integrated story that actively strengthens the case for fit.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Ongoing adversarial skill-building outside ordinary product work, especially through CTFs or similar hands-on exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual CTF participation or similar practice.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows strong competitive results or especially serious, ongoing offensive-security practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Responsibility for or contribution to public codebases, including maintainership or externally accountable engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: The technical ambition, rigor, and seriousness of self-directed projects outside formal work responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Motivation toward foundational infrastructure or shared tooling whose benefits compound across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production ownership breadth
features.description: The breadth and depth of hands-on production delivery experience shown through launches, maintenance, operational responsibility, and service ownership.

levels.descriptor: Describes launching or owning only a small number of production services, such as 2.
Describes a moderate shipped footprint, such as about 4 production services.
Describes repeated launch and maintenance experience across many services, such as 6 or more.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How deeply and credibly the letter shows Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Relevant software tenure
features.description: The amount or duration of directly relevant professional software engineering experience the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Reliability mindset
features.description: A bias toward maintainability, operability, failure awareness, and long-term system care rather than feature delivery alone.

levels.descriptor: Shows little attention to maintainability or resilience.
Uses generic reliability language without much depth.
Shows a clear maintainer or resilience-oriented framing.
Backs a reliability mindset with concrete attention to failure cases, inherited systems, or stewardship.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: How specifically and persuasively the letter connects the applicant's background and motivations to this exact role, team mandate, or posted requirements.

levels.descriptor: Shows little role-specific motivation beyond wanting a software job or a brand-name employer.
Mentions security, scale, or Google in broad terms without a strong personal rationale.
Gives a clear role-relevant reason for interest, such as secure-by-default tooling or scaling scarce security effort.
Presents a precise, memorable thesis for wanting this role that is tightly tied to the team's mandate and the applicant's own priorities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Hands-on experience reviewing systems, code, or designs for security issues and following findings through remediation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: How well the letter understands the role or problem as scaling security expertise through tooling, workflow design, and automation.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security credentials
features.description: The strength of formal external security certifications or credentialing presented as validation of security knowledge or skill.

levels.descriptor: No formal security credential is mentioned.
A baseline credential is mentioned, such as Security+, indicating foundational security study.
A stronger hands-on credential is mentioned, such as OSCP, indicating practical offensive testing ability.

features.name: Security philosophy and rigor
features.description: The applicant's articulated point of view about what security engineering is for and the standards of care it demands.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinct philosophy about the quality bar required for security engineering.
Makes only generic statements about reliability or security importance.
Expresses a clear philosophy of quiet resilience, dependable systems, or a higher standard for security tooling.
Builds a memorable, well-integrated case that security tooling demands exceptional rigor and ties that belief to prior work or design choices.

features.name: Upstream repair habit
features.description: A habit of fixing defects in dependencies or tools at their source upstream rather than only working around them locally.

levels.descriptor: No upstream fixing behavior is shown.
Mentions occasional or general patch submission.
Shows a recurring habit of diagnosing defects and sending corrective patches upstream.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Direct ownership of tooling that automates vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: Shows no vulnerability-handling workflow experience.
Mentions vulnerability work but not ownership of the automation around it.
Describes building automation for a vulnerability intake or triage queue.
Describes a richer pipeline with features such as classification, deduplication, routing, prioritization, or clear workload reduction.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Proofreading quality and sentence-level mechanical professionalism, including spelling, grammar, and copy-editing accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: Dimensions that are genuinely hybrid or idiosyncratic and do not cleanly match one recurring evaluative construct.

levels.descriptor: No security engagement outside day-job claims is shown.
A modest external signal is shown, such as casual CTF participation or a baseline security credential.
A strong external signal is shown, such as serious competitive CTF results or a hands-on credential like OSCP.
Multiple strong external signals are shown, such as both high-level CTF performance and a hands-on offensive certification.
